1: Huineng was poor, and sold firewood to keep his mother. When he heard a guest reciting the Diamond Sutra, his heart opened at once. He came to the monastery at Huangmei, and the Fifth Patriarch asked: You are from the south, from the land of barbarians — how dare you seek Buddhahood? Huineng answered: People may be north or south, but is the Buddha-nature north or south? There is no north or south in Buddha-nature.

The head monk Shenxiu wrote on the wall: The body is the bodhi-tree, the mind is a standing mirror. At all times we must wipe it, and let no dust alight. And the illiterate rice-pounder Huineng had his verse read aloud: Bodhi has no tree, the mirror has no stand; Buddha-nature is forever pure — where could dust alight? That night the Patriarch gave him the robe and the bowl.
[Platform Sutra, ch. 1 — Not mind, not Buddha]

Shenxiu's school teaches that the mirror must be polished daily. Huineng's teaches that there is nothing to polish. Between the two verses lies the whole quarrel of the schools — and both point at the same moon.
2: [Platform Sutra, ch. 2 — Prajna for the great and the small]

The bodhisattva precepts say: Be always and everywhere in practice. Good friends, the prajna wisdom is originally in yourselves — do not doubt it. The small in capacity, hearing this, may awaken as quickly as the great; for delusion and awakening are not two. Only the deluded take long; the awakened find it now.

My teaching takes no-thought as its doctrine: no-thought means not to be stained by the world of things. Thought is the nature of man; the world is the occasion of thought. To think of good and evil without being bound by good and evil — that is the walking of the path.
[Platform Sutra, ch. 2 — The flags in the wind]

At Guangzhou two monks were arguing by the temple flag: one said the flag moves, the other said the wind moves. Huineng came and said: It is not the wind that moves, nor the flag — it is your minds that move. And the whole company was struck with awe.
3: When Huineng knew his time had come, his disciples wept. He said: You weep because you do not know where I go; if you knew, you would not weep. All things are impermanent — this is the nature of things. Sit in quiet, and do not weep as worldly people weep.

From the first, not a thing is. If not a thing is, what is there to attain? Good friends, each of you must see your own nature; do not go looking for the buddha outside. The buddha of the past, the buddha of the future, the buddha of the present — all are in your own body.

And sitting upright, Huineng said: Goodbye to you all — and passed quietly away in the third watch of the night. A white rainbow rose from the room, and the mountain wept with a strange fragrance, and the wood of the forest turned white. The priest who is always present is not in a body; the teaching does not die with the teacher.
